title: Gallipoli Campaign - ANZAC Landing
description: On April 25, 1915, Australian and New Zealand Army Corps (ANZAC) forces landed at Gallipoli Peninsula, Turkey, in a failed attempt to capture Constantinople and secure a sea route to Russia during World War I. The eight-month campaign resulted in over 44,000 Allied deaths (including 8,700 Australians and 2,700 New Zealanders) and 57,000 Turkish deaths. Despite the military failure, Gallipoli became a defining moment in Australian and New Zealand national identity. April 25 is commemorated as ANZAC Day, the most significant day of remembrance in both nations.
